svg.title: The experiment
svg.text: MPX SPIN V1 (CONCEPT 04 DEVELOPED) · DESIGN REVIEW

text.tspan: Does spinning a cylindrical filter make water pass faster than gravity? 200 mL per trial, three trials at three conditions (MPx_01, pp. 76–79).

svg.text: The rig: Ø50 × 150 mm cage, PWM board
RESULTS, TIME FOR 200 ML TO PASS (S)

text.tspan: A · motor off
B · 3,500 rpm
Spinning cut the time from 22.4 s to 6.8 s:
the baseline. The team's notes: RPM was not verified,
removal and water quality were not measured, loading and clogging not tested.
106 L/h is how fast one batch drains,
not what a user gets. Add the pour and the stop and the rig's cycle
is about
33 L/h
3.3× faster at 5,000 rpm is far too little.
If the water turned with the basket, the pressure at the wall
would be about 60× the static head.
A 25 µm paper is a pre-filter
for microplastics. By count most particles are under 20 µm; it catches about
SD at motor-off is 2.4 s
(11 %): the start and stop of the timing matters as much as the speed.

Time until the water has passed and collected
below
